The account setup process defines a causal chain of infrastructure dependencies. Each step must complete before the next can begin. The domain registration (Step 1) is foundational because it enables secure communication channels required by Stripe webhooks and Google OAuth. Hosting (Vercel) requires the domain to be established first. The managed Postgres instance (Step 3) needs to be configured with a region aligned to Vercel’s default for latency optimization. Google OAuth credentials (Step 5) require the domain to define authorized origins. These dependencies form a directed acyclic graph (DAG), where each node represents a functional component and edges represent temporal and logical precedence. Failure at any stage blocks subsequent stages. For example, without a valid domain, Stripe webhooks cannot be configured. The system's robustness depends on enforcing this order. The environment variables produced at each step become inputs to downstream systems, forming a feedback loop of configuration integrity. The sequence ensures that all necessary services are provisioned before runtime begins.
